title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو في زيارة لدولة الكويت
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew on a Visit to the State of Kuwait
body_ar:
يقوم الشيخ محمد الحسن بن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بزيارة للكويت، وخلال هذه الزيارة ألقى الشيخ محاضرة قيمة ضمن فعاليات جائزة الكويت الدولية لحفظ القرآن الكريم ، وبالتنسيق مع وزارة الأوقاف الكويتية .

المحاضرة التي نقلت مباشرة على "قناة إثراء" الكويتية ، تحدث فيها الشيخ باستفاضة ،

عن المعاني الجليلة التي يزخر بها كتاب الله ، كما تحدث عن المكانة العالية التي يحتلها هذا الكتاب ، الذي هو خلاصة وخاتم الكتب السماوية ..

كما تطرق فضيلة الشيخ للمعاني والفيوضات الربانية ، التي يجنيها المشتغلون بهذا الكتاب ؛ دراسة وتلاوة وتدبرا ؛ كما ذكر الشيخ ؛ أن هذا القرآن يضم بين دفتيه دواء لكل الأمراض المستعصية في هذا العصر ، وأن هذا مجرب علمه من علمه ، وجهله من جهله ، وذكر الشيخ تعامل السلف الصالح من صحابة وتابعين مع هذا القرآن

لأنهم فهموا حقيقته ومكانته ،ضاربا المثل بالخليفة الراشد عمر ابن الخطاب رضي الله عنه الذي كان وقافا عند كتاب الله ، فبهذا القرآن يقول الشيخ : تنال معية الله وتتنزل الرحمات ، وتشفى الأنفس والأبدان ، ذاكرا قصة أسيد بن حضير رضي الله عنه الواردة في الصحيحين وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم له : (تِلكَ السَّكِينَةُ تَنَزَّلتْ للقُرآنِ) .

وفي سياق متصل نظمت رابطة الجالية الموريتانية في دولة الكويت ندوة تحت عنوان:

"المغتربون والفرص المتاحة" أنعشها كوكبة من العلماء الأجلاء وهم :

الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو ، ومحمد عبد الرحمن ولد أحمد الملقب "ولد فتى" ، وفضيلة القارئ الإمام : شيخنا ولد سيد الحاج .
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan bin al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, is making a visit to Kuwait. During this visit the Sheikh delivered a valuable lecture within the proceedings of the Kuwait International Prize for the Memorisation of the Noble Qur'an, in coordination with the Kuwaiti Ministry of Endowments.

The lecture, which was broadcast live on the Kuwaiti channel 'Ithraa', was one in which the Sheikh spoke at length,

about the majestic meanings with which the Book of God abounds. He also spoke of the lofty standing this Book occupies, being the summation and the seal of the revealed Books…

His Eminence the Sheikh also touched on the meanings and the divine outpourings gathered by those who occupy themselves with this Book — in study, in recitation and in reflection. The Sheikh mentioned that this Qur'an holds between its two covers a remedy for every intractable disease of this age, and that this has been tested: whoever has known it has known it, and whoever has been ignorant of it has been ignorant of it. The Sheikh mentioned how the righteous forebears, among the Companions and the generation that followed them, dealt with this Qur'an

because they understood its reality and its standing — citing as an example the rightly-guided caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him), who would halt at the Book of God. By this Qur'an, the Sheikh says, God's companionship is attained, mercies descend, and souls and bodies are healed. He mentioned the story of Usayd ibn Hudayr (may God be pleased with him) that appears in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, and the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to him: 'That was the tranquillity (sakīnah) that descended for the Qur'an.'

In a related context, the Association of the Mauritanian Community in the State of Kuwait organised a symposium under the title:

'Expatriates and the Opportunities Available', enlivened by a company of distinguished scholars, namely:

Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew; Muhammad Abd al-Rahman Ould Ahmad, known as 'Ould Fata'; and His Eminence the reciter and imam Shaykhna Ould Sidi al-Hajj.

flags.context: the report of Usayd ibn Hudayr, attributed by the reporter to the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections
options: That was the tranquillity (sakīnah) that descended for the Qur'an
That was the divine presence that came down for the Qur'an
That was the sakīnah, which descended on account of the Qur'an
flags.note: السكينة is a Qur'anic term (e.g. Sūrat al-Fatḥ 48:4) with no single English equivalent; 'tranquillity' is the usual rendering but loses the sense of a descending divine presence. 'للقرآن' may be causal ('on account of') or purposive ('for'). The attribution to al-Bukhari and Muslim is the reporter's and is preserved exactly as given, with no grading added (style guide §4).

flags.arabic: وأن هذا مجرب علمه من علمه ، وجهله من جهله
flags.context: the Sheikh on the Qur'an as a remedy
options: this has been tested: whoever has known it has known it, and whoever has been ignorant of it has been ignorant of it
this is proven by experience — known to those who know it and unknown to those who do not
flags.note: An Arabic rhetorical formula that does not carry over. The literal rendering is kept so that nothing is added; option 1 reads better but smooths an assertion the Sheikh made in a deliberately terse form.

flags.context: the example of the caliph Umar
options: who would halt at the Book of God
who would stop short at the limits of the Book of God
who held fast to the Book of God
flags.note: 'وقّاف عند كتاب الله' is an established idiom for one who stops wherever Scripture sets a limit and goes no further. The literal 'halt at' preserves the image; a reviewer may prefer option 1, which is clearer but adds words the Arabic does not have.

translator_notes: News report of a lecture. The lecture itself is not on this page. 'وزارة الأوقاف الكويتية' is Kuwait's Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs; rendered as 'Ministry of Endowments' to match the glossary for waqf. Mauritanian personal names kept in their Mauritanian forms (Ould). The source's paragraph breaks fall mid-sentence in two places and have been kept where they fall. CMS date is a bulk-upload timestamp, not a composition date.
